prompt: Stage 5-1, level 8, 20 HP, five players left. Your plan this round was floor 0, stop when Lillia and Morgana are both 2-star. Forty gold in, Lillia is 2-star, Morgana is still 1-star with a second copy on the bench, and 12 gold is left. Seat 3 holds a 2-star Morgana and is your next opponent; scouting says you still lose to them with the current board. A loss now costs about 18. Do you roll the last 12?

lobby.note: Morgana 2-star; your next opponent, beats you even with Lillia 2-star

options.label: Yes, all six shops now: the floor was 0 and the stop condition is not met
No, keep the 12: Lillia 2-star is enough of a stabilise, and at 5-2 you roll nine shops with 18 gold
No, put the 12 into XP: level 9 at 5-3 is the only way a board this far behind catches up

explanation:
Start with what 12 gold is worth next round. Held, it earns 1 interest and you fight 5-1 with a 1-star carry against a board you lose to: 20 minus 18 leaves 2 HP, and at 5-2 a bag of 18 gold is nine shops that have to hit and then win every fight for the rest of the game. Gold has no future when the HP has none.

Six shops now is not hopeless. Ten Morgana exist, you hold two, Seat 3 holds three, so five remain in a 4-cost pool of roughly 115: 0.30 times 5 over 115 is 1.3% per slot, about 6% per shop, and six shops land the copy about one time in three. A 2-star Morgana with three items turns the next fight from a loss into a real fight, worth far more than 1 gold and nine shops at 2 HP. Stopping because Lillia hit is the classic rolldown failure: you found something, so you will finish next round. XP is the same mistake with a bigger number: a level 50 XP away helps nobody this round.
principle: One more roll is worth it when the gold has no next round: count the losses left before you count the interest.
commonMistake: Stopping the rolldown at the first hit and saving the rest for a next round that HP says you will not have.
hint: Take 18 from 20, then ask what the 12 gold could buy in the round that follows.
